one_liner: POWER8+ vpmsum carry-less-multiply CRC32/CRC32C kernel in assembly (and intrinsics C); 41x a slice-by-8 table CRC on 32 kB.
what_it_does: Computes a 32-bit CRC for any polynomial on POWER8 and later (ppc64 and ppc64le) using the vector polynomial multiply-sum instructions. You run `make` once to generate a constants header for your polynomial (CRC32C with reflection and xor-out by default, Ethernet CRC32 and CRC32K examples in the Makefile), then copy four files (crc32.S, crc32_wrapper.c, the constants header, ppc-opcode.h) or the single-file intrinsics version (vec_crc32.c) into your build. The API is one function, `unsigned int crc32_vpmsum(unsigned int crc, unsigned char *p, unsigned long len)`, whose name can be changed with -DCRC32_FUNCTION so several polynomials can coexist.
how_it_is_fast: CRC folding with carry-less multiplication: the main loop keeps 8 independent 16-byte accumulators (8 x 16 B per iteration) to hide the 6-cycle vpmsumd latency at one issue per cycle, folds up to 32 kB (MAX_SIZE) down to 1024 bits with precomputed x^n mod P constants, reduces 1024 bits to 64, then finishes with a fixed-point Barrett reduction. Bit-reflected CRCs are handled by loading bytes reversed (vperm) instead of reflecting bits. Unaligned heads, tails and inputs under 31 bytes go through a byte-at-a-time Sarwate table loop in the C wrapper; inputs of 16 to 255 aligned bytes use a separate short path with per-length constants.
when_to_use: CRC32C (iSCSI, ext4/btrfs, Ceph, RocksDB style) or zlib/Ethernet CRC32 on IBM POWER8, POWER9 or POWER10 Linux, buffers of hundreds of bytes and up.
Storage or network paths that checksum 4 kB to multi-MB blocks, where a table-driven CRC costs about 3 cycles per byte on POWER8 (0.33 bytes/cycle in the README's slice-by-8 run).
You need a non-standard 32-bit polynomial accelerated: crc32_constants generates the folding and Barrett constants for any polynomial, reflected or not.
Codebases that cannot pull in a whole crypto or compression library and want a small, dual-licensed (Apache-2.0 or GPL-2.0+) source drop.
when_not_to_use: Any non-POWER target, or POWER7 and older: the code needs the ISA 2.07 vpmsum instructions and has no portable fallback beyond a byte-wise table loop; check AT_HWCAP2 & PPC_FEATURE2_VEC_CRYPTO at run time yourself.

Tiny inputs: below 31 bytes the wrapper runs a one-byte-per-step table loop, slower than slice-by-8; the Linux kernel's glue only enters the vector path at 528 bytes or more (VECTOR_BREAKPOINT 512 plus 16) and uses the table code below that.

If you already use zlib-ng (arch/power/crc32_power8.c), Go's hash/crc32 on ppc64le, the Linux kernel, Ceph or RocksDB on POWER: each ships a derived copy of this code, so vendoring it again gains nothing.
You need CRC-64, CRC-16/T10-DIF or crc32_combine: the generator covers 32-bit CRCs only and there is no combine function (issue #10 asked for one).
Projects that need active upstream maintenance: no commits since 2020-03-26.

integration.dependencies: none at run time; the constants header is generated at build time by the repo's crc32_constants tool (buildable on non-POWER hosts for cross builds)
integration.min_toolchain: GCC or Clang targeting POWER8 with -mcpu=power8 -mcrypto -mpower8-vector -maltivec -mvsx (Clang 7+ needed the 2020 workaround in clang_workaround.h); exact minimum versions not documented
integration.platforms: ppc64 and ppc64le Linux, POWER8 or later (vpmsum required); big- and little-endian both handled
integration.thread_safety: Stateless pure function over caller memory (running CRC passed in and returned), so reentrant; not otherwise documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same CRC result as a table-driven CRC for the polynomial the header was generated for, but under its own function name and signature, and only after generating constants per polynomial; the repo's slice-by-8 baseline computes a different CRC (big-endian 0x04C11DB7) than the default build (reflected CRC32C)

gotchas: Only one size was ever measured: the 41x figure is for a 32 kB page-aligned buffer, which is exactly the kernel's MAX_SIZE fold block (the best case, one block, no head or tail work); no numbers exist for small, unaligned or multi-block inputs, and the repo's own vec_crc32_bench (intrinsics C) has no published figure, so the gain of hand-written assembly over the intrinsics version is unknown.

The baseline is slice-by-8 for a different polynomial and bit order (big-endian Ethernet CRC32 versus reflected CRC32C) built at the Makefile's -O2; it ran at about 1.34 GB/s (0.33 bytes/cycle, derived from page data), so a stronger table method such as slice-by-16 or zlib's braided CRC would narrow the gap. The slice-by-8 harness was refactored in 2017 (commit aadb491) after the README numbers, but its inner loop is unchanged.
The 3.8x btrfs figure in the README does not match the Linux commit 6dd7a82cc54e message, which (per search-result text, page not opened) says 'over 3.7x faster' for a dd 4 GiB btrfs write test.

The assembly saves non-volatile vector and GPR registers below the stack pointer (in the ABI's protected zone) and reads constants TOC-relative through r2; Ceph's separate crc32c_ppc_fast_zero_asm.S, not this repo's crc32.S, broke with a relocation-out-of-range error in shared libraries (issue #14, fixed in ceph#59558). The intrinsics C version gave wrong results on big-endian ppc64 with Clang until commit c520cfb (2018).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libgcrypt, Nettle or CRYPTOGAMS when you need only a POWER CRC32/CRC32C (or a custom 32-bit polynomial) as a few vendorable files rather than a whole crypto library; none of the other catalogued hand-written kernels in this category targets CRC on POWER.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README run: 5,000,000 CRC32C passes over one 32 kB L1-resident buffer took 2.937 s with the vpmsum assembly versus 122.220 s for a Linux-kernel-derived slice-by-8 C table CRC (different polynomial, Makefile -O2, compiler version unstated), about 41.6x, or 52 GiB/s and 13.6 bytes/cycle on an unnamed 4.1 GHz POWER8, timed with shell `time`.
status_note: Dormant since 2020-03-26 (54 commits, one open issue about a Ceph-side file) but small, dual Apache-2.0/GPL-2.0+ licensed and copyable; the same algorithm lives on, maintained, in mainline Linux (lib/crc/powerpc), Go hash/crc32, zlib-ng, Ceph and RocksDB.
